cases.prompt: The function name and types are clear, but callers cannot tell that loading the same partition key replaces the previous load. Clarify this in the source file without changing code behavior.
assertions: Uses a docstring or equivalent code-adjacent caller-facing explanation for the non-obvious contract.
Does not rename the function, change its signature, or refactor executable code.
Avoids repeating information already obvious from the name and types.

cases.prompt: Cleanup must happen after result capture so cleanup failure never replaces the original result or exception. The code is correct but the reason is not obvious. Clarify it without changing executable code.
assertions: Uses a concise code-local comment to explain why the ordering matters.
Does not rewrite the control flow when the code itself is already appropriate.
Explains rationale rather than translating the next statement into prose.

cases.prompt: This source module follows a local convention that is essential to maintainers but not visible from any one symbol. Add the smallest source-level explanation without duplicating the architecture guide.
assertions: May use a module-level explanation when the convention is genuinely local to the source file.
Projects only the local information maintainers need instead of copying broader policy.
Does not change executable code.

cases.prompt: This function uses positional tuples, overloaded booleans, and three meaningless wrappers. Add comments so it becomes understandable.
assertions: Does not use comments to cover a comprehension problem caused by executable code structure or representation.
Routes the structural refactor to code-comprehension-refactor.
Does not modify executable code under clarify-code.

cases.prompt: Add comments before every line explaining what each statement does.
assertions: Rejects or minimizes comments that merely restate obvious code.
Adds prose only where it supplies non-obvious caller contract or maintainer rationale.

cases.prompt: Rewrite all source comments for style, including noqa, type: ignore, coverage pragmas, formatter directives, and the encoding cookie.
assertions: Does not treat machine-consumed directives or source metadata as ordinary explanatory comments.
Preserves tooling and runtime contracts unless their semantics are explicitly part of the task and validated.

cases.prompt: Improve a docstring that is also used by doctest and reflected into generated API documentation. Keep behavior and tooling output semantics intact.
assertions: Recognizes that the docstring is an observable or tool-consumed surface rather than inert prose.
Preserves doctest and documentation contract semantics and uses relevant validation before claiming preservation.
Still avoids changing executable code.

cases.prompt: The code and naming are already clear. Add one more explanatory comment for readability without changing the code.
assertions: May choose a no-op when the requested comment would not remove non-obvious inference, search, or misunderstanding cost.
Does not treat comment quantity as a readability or quality proxy.
Does not invent rationale or contracts that are not supported by the code or context.

cases.prompt: A simpler caching approach looks tempting, but it would hide permission changes that must become visible within the same request. The implementation is already correct. Clarify this for future maintainers without changing executable code.
assertions: May preserve the current constraint and consequence as a code-local comment because it prevents a likely but invalid future change.
Explains the current invariant rather than recording discussion history or a rejected proposal log.
Keeps the explanation tied to the narrow surface where the caching decision matters.

cases.prompt: Only one branch requires validation to happen before cleanup, but I want a long module docstring saying validation must always precede cleanup. Clarify the reason without changing code.
assertions: Does not broaden a branch-local ordering constraint into a module-wide rule.
Prefers an explanation near the affected branch or ordering when that is the actual semantic scope.
Keeps broader module-level documentation free of a false global invariant.

cases.prompt: A comment still names an old variable and describes a previous three-step algorithm, but the real invariant that cleanup must not replace the original error is still valid. Improve the explanation without changing executable code.
assertions: Does not merely polish stale implementation narration.
Rewrites or reduces the comment around the current durable invariant and consequence, or removes obsolete details that add no value.
Does not change executable code while correcting the explanation.
